title: Git Basics - init
content:
# Git Basics: `git init`

`git init` creates a new Git repository in the current directory.

## Usage
```bash
git init
```

## Notes
- Creates a `.git/` folder to track history
- Only needs to be run once per project

title: Git Basics - clone
content:
# Git Basics: `git clone`

`git clone` copies a remote repository to your local machine.

## Usage
```bash
git clone https://github.com/user/repo.git
```

## Notes
- Downloads all files and commit history
- Sets up remote called `origin`

title: Git Basics - add
content:
# Git Basics: `git add`

`git add` stages changes for the next commit.

## Usage
```bash
git add file.txt
# or stage all changes
git add .
```

title: Git Basics - commit
content:
# Git Basics: `git commit`

`git commit` saves staged changes to the repository history.

## Usage
```bash
git commit -m "Your commit message"
```

## Tip
Write clear, descriptive commit messages.

title: Git Basics - status
content:
# Git Basics: `git status`

`git status` shows the current state of the working directory and staging area.

## Usage
```bash
git status
```

title: Git Basics - log
content:
# Git Basics: `git log`

`git log` shows the commit history.

## Usage
```bash
git log --oneline
```

title: Git Basics - branch
content:
# Git Basics: `git branch`

`git branch` lists, creates, or deletes branches.

## Usage
```bash
git branch        # list branches
git branch feature # create branch
```

title: Git Basics - checkout/switch
content:
# Git Basics: Switching branches

Use `git switch` (modern) or `git checkout` to change branches.

## Usage
```bash
git switch feature
# or
git checkout feature
```

title: Git Basics - merge
content:
# Git Basics: `git merge`

`git merge` combines changes from another branch into the current branch.

## Usage
```bash
git switch main
git merge feature
```

title: Git Basics - push/pull
content:
# Git Basics: push & pull

- `git push` sends local commits to remote
- `git pull` fetches and merges remote changes

## Usage
```bash
git push origin main
git pull origin main
```
